title: Forward a terminal's request as the switch, and answer it as the terminal's

blocks.text: The switch now also forwards purchases and balance inquiries from fuel-station terminals to `fleet`, a fuel-card network, as well as to `visa`. The fleet network knows the switch as one terminal, `SW000001`, sent by acquirer `12345678901`, and refuses any message that carries the terminals' private field 48. The terminals match answers the way any QMUX does. A purchase's approval must show the network's approval code, and an inquiry's the balance the network returned (field 54). Nothing else in the network's answer is for the terminal.

`ForwardLeg` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/ForwardLeg.java` already holds the two participants that stand around `QueryHost` in the forwarding group. Finish the three methods marked `TODO`: `outbound`, `reply` and `nextStan`. About fifteen lines in total.

The tests deploy a real TransactionManager, a real `QueryHost` and two real QMUXes with Q2, in the test's own JVM, with a scripted network behind each QMUX. After the group, an abort participant answers reported failures from the terminal's request, as unit s10's does. Besides approvals, the tests send declines, purchases the network never answers, and two purchases in flight at once.

cases.says: an approved purchase reaches the network under the switch's terminal and acquirer IDs, without field 48, and the terminal gets the approval with its approval code
an approved balance inquiry gives the terminal the balance the network returned
a decline and a silent network are answered with the terminal's own STAN and terminal ID, because the request the answers start from was never renumbered
the approval is built from the terminal's request, so the network's private field and the switch's acquirer ID never reach the terminal
each network link has its own STAN sequence, unaffected by traffic on the other link
two terminals that use the same STAN at once are both answered, because the switch numbers what it sends

origin.section: 16.1 The Destination Gets a Copy Numbered by the Switch, and Every Answer Starts From the Source's Request

concepts: The destination receives a copy of the source's request; every answer to the source, approval, decline or 91 alike, is built from the unchanged request, so renumbering the request in place breaks every answer.
On each upstream link the switch is the sender, so the copy carries a STAN from one sequence per destination link and the switch's own identifiers.
